definition: A modern, high-performance web framework for building APIs with Python using standard Python type hints. Built on Starlette and Pydantic.
The ASGI web framework that FastAPI is built on top of. Provides routing, middleware, WebSocket support, and other web features.
The data validation library that FastAPI uses for request/response data handling. Uses Python type annotations for validation and serialization.
The ASGI server used to run FastAPI applications. An implementation of the ASGI specification.
Asynchronous Server Gateway Interface — the asynchronous successor to WSGI for Python web applications.
A dynamic value in the URL path (e.g., {item_id}) that is extracted and passed to the endpoint function.
An optional parameter passed in the URL query string (e.g., ?q=somequery) and parsed by FastAPI.
Data sent to the server, typically in JSON format, validated against a Pydantic model.
A Pydantic model that defines the structure, types, and validation of API responses.
A combination of an HTTP method and a URL path that defines an API endpoint. Decorated with @app.get(), @app.post(), etc.
FastAPI's system for declaring and managing dependencies that are automatically resolved and injected into path operations.
Standard Python type annotations used by FastAPI for automatic validation, serialization, and documentation.
A standard for describing the structure of JSON data. FastAPI automatically generates JSON Schema for models.
The standard specification used for automatic API documentation generation in FastAPI.
An interactive API documentation interface automatically generated by FastAPI at /docs.
An alternative interactive API documentation interface generated by FastAPI at /redoc.
A function that processes every request before it is handled by a path operation and every response before returning it.
Cross-Origin Resource Sharing — a mechanism that allows restricted resources on a web page to be requested from another domain.
A protocol providing full-duplex communication channels over a single TCP connection. Supported natively by FastAPI.
A task that runs after returning a response, useful for operations that don't need to complete before the response.
An authorization framework supported by FastAPI's security utilities for token-based authentication.
JSON Web Token — a compact, self-contained token format for securely transmitting information between parties.
An exception class that returns an HTTP error response with a specific status code and detail message.
An HTTP response status code (e.g., 200, 404, 500) indicating the result of the request.
